newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ASC says Coles Myer papers safe.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ASC says Coles Myer papers safe.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission on Tuesday denied intruders who broke into its Melbourne offices at the weekend had taken or copied files linked with retailing giant Coles Myer Ltd.
The corporate watchdog, which is investigating a share transaction involving the group, said the intruders won access to an area where only publicly available documents were kept.
"The intruders that did get into the building got nowhere near the Yannon documents," said spokesman Steven Blaney, referring to the so-called Yannon transaction.
The 1990 Yannon deal cost Coles Myer A$18 million and benefitted a company associated with former chairman and major shareholder Solomon Lew, by a similar sum.
"The Yannon documents were held in a secure room in another part of the building," Blaney told Reuters.
Earlier, the Herald-Sun newspaper reported the intruders "spied" on the Yannon documents.
Australian Federal Police are investigating the break-in.
